title: Too much work to stop now
situation: You spent two weekends building a strategy and testing it on simulated practice charts. Over 100 simulated trades it lost money after costs like the [[spread]], and you cannot find a rule that clearly fixes it. You do not want to give up because of all the time you put in.
question: What do you do next?

responses.text: Start trading it on your demo account anyway. You have invested too much to stop.
responses.explanation: The time you spent is gone whichever way you choose. Continuing because of it is called the sunk cost trap.

responses.text: Keep changing rules until the backtest shows a profit.
responses.explanation: Changing rules until past results look good can produce a strategy that only fits that one set of data.

responses.text: Write down what you learned from the test, set the strategy aside, and start from a fresh idea.
responses.explanation: The test gave you a clear answer, which is useful. Your notes keep the lessons even though the strategy did not work.

responses.text: Leave it for a month and look at it again then.
responses.explanation: Some distance can help you think clearly, but it does not change what the test showed.

takeaway: Time already spent is gone either way. Decide based on what the evidence shows now.
